neet_che_u18_t04_1.working: Arenediazonium salts are stable only at low temperature. On warming in aqueous solution they decompose to phenol and N2, so the reaction is kept at 273-278 K.

neet_che_u18_t04_2.working: This is the Balz-Schiemann reaction. HBF4 precipitates the diazonium fluoroborate, and heating that salt gives fluorobenzene plus BF3 and N2.

neet_che_u18_t04_3.working: Bromine water converts aniline to 2,4,6-tribromoaniline. Diazotisation followed by H3PO2 replaces the diazonium group with H, leaving 1,3,5-tribromobenzene.

neet_che_u18_t04_4.working: Alkyldiazonium salts are less stable than arenediazonium salts, so A is false. Arenediazonium ions are stabilised by resonance with the ring, so R is true.

neet_che_u18_t04_5.working: I: CuCN/KCN gives PhCN, and LiAlH4 reduces it to PhCH2NH2 (benzylamine), so I is correct. II: coupling with aniline in mildly acidic medium gives yellow p-aminoazobenzene with the -N=N- linkage retained, so II is correct.
